config.title: useId & Stable IDs

intro.title: useId & Stable IDs
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form with multiple input fields, each requiring a unique ID for accessibility and functionality. You will learn the core concept of generating stable, unique IDs using Angular's `useId` function to prevent ID collisions and ensure consistent behavior across renders. The main technologies involved are Angular components, TypeScript, and the `useId` API from Angular's core utilities. This beginner-friendly lesson will guide you through implementing stable IDs step-by-step, helping you understand why they are important for forms and other UI elements.
intro.usecase: In real-world Angular applications, generating stable unique IDs is essential for accessibility and form functionality. When building complex forms with multiple input fields, each label needs a reliable `for` attribute that matches its corresponding input's `id`. This pattern appears in user registration forms, checkout flows, and data entry dashboards where screen readers must correctly associate labels with inputs. Developers also use stable IDs for ARIA attributes in dynamic components like accordions, tab panels, and modal dialogs to maintain consistent accessibility across component re-renders.

objectives: Implement the useId hook to generate unique identifiers within Angular components
Apply stable IDs to form elements for proper accessibility labeling
Configure component properties to accept custom ID prefixes
Bind generated IDs to HTML attributes like 'for' and 'id' in templates
Initialize multiple stable IDs within a single component instance
Render dynamic content with guaranteed unique identifiers across re-renders
Integrate useId with Angular's change detection for consistent ID persistence

steps.title: Import Component and useId from Angular core
steps.instruction: Import Component and useId from '@angular/core' in your component file.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to bring in both symbols from the Angular core module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing from a module
import { Component, OnInit } from '@angular/core';
steps.expectedOutcome: The component file will have the necessary imports for creating an Angular component and using the useId hook.
successCriteria: Component and useId are imported from '@angular/core'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both Component and useId from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import both Component and useId from the '@angular/core' module.

steps.title: Create the main component class with Component decorator
steps.instruction: Define a component class named 'StableIdDemo' and decorate it with @Component. Set the selector to 'app-stable-id-demo' and the template to an empty string for now.
steps.hint: Use the imported Component decorator and define a class with the given name and decorator.

seedCode.App.tsx:
import { Component, useId } from '@angular/core';

// Define the StableIdDemo component class here

steps.expectedOutcome: A component class named StableIdDemo is created with the @Component decorator, selector, and empty template.
successCriteria: The StableIdDemo class is defined, decorated with @Component, has selector 'app-stable-id-demo', and template set to empty string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the class is named 'StableIdDemo', has the @Component decorator with selector 'app-stable-id-demo' and template ''.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class isn't properly defined. Check that you're using the @Component decorator with the correct selector and template.

steps.title: Initialize a stable ID using useId hook
steps.instruction: Inside the StableIdDemo component class, declare a property named 'stableId' and assign it the result of calling the useId() hook.
steps.hint: Add a property declaration in the component class body, like 'stableId = useId();'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class now has a 'stableId' property containing a unique string generated by useId().
successCriteria: Property 'stableId' is declared
useId() is called to initialize it
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useId() and assigning the result to a property named 'stableId'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The stableId property wasn't properly initialized with useId(). Check the syntax: 'stableId = useId();' inside the class.

steps.title: Store the generated ID in a component property
steps.instruction: Inside the StableIdDemo class, assign the result of calling useId() to a public property named stableId.
steps.hint: You can assign the useId() call directly to a class property. Make sure the property is public so it can be accessed from the template.
steps.expectedOutcome: The stableId property will be initialized with a unique, stable identifier that can be used in the template.
successCriteria: The StableIdDemo class has a public stableId property assigned with the result of useId().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're assigning the result of useId() to a public property named stableId.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a public stableId property in the StableIdDemo class and assign it the value returned by useId().

steps.title: Add basic template structure with header
steps.instruction: Add a header element to the component's template that displays the lesson title 'Stable ID Demo'.
steps.hint: Use an <h1> element inside the template string with the text content 'Stable ID Demo'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now contains an <h1> element with the text 'Stable ID Demo'.
successCriteria: The template string includes an <h1> element
The <h1> contains the text 'Stable ID Demo'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added an <h1> element with exactly 'Stable ID Demo' as its content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template should contain an <h1> element with the text 'Stable ID Demo'. Check that you've added it correctly.

steps.title: Display the generated stable ID in the template
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add a paragraph element that displays the stableId property using interpolation.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to bind the stableId property value into the template.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will show the generated stable ID value when rendered.
successCriteria: The template contains a paragraph element with interpolation displaying the stableId property value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using interpolation syntax {{ }} to display the stableId property value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The stableId property isn't being displayed in the template. Check that you've added a paragraph with interpolation.

steps.title: Add an input element to demonstrate ID usage
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add an input element with a label that uses the stableId property for the input's id attribute.
steps.hint: Use the stableId property to bind to the input's id attribute. The label should have a 'for' attribute that matches this id.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will contain an input element with a label, demonstrating how to use the stable ID for accessibility.
successCriteria: Input element is present in the template
Label has 'for' attribute bound to stableId
Input has 'id' attribute bound to stableId
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an input element, but make sure both the label's 'for' attribute and the input's 'id' attribute use the stableId property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element or its accessibility attributes are missing. Add an input with a label that uses the stableId for both 'for' and 'id' attributes.

steps.title: Wire the stable ID to input's id and label's for attributes
steps.instruction: In the template, add a label element with a 'for' attribute bound to your stableId property, and update the input element to have an 'id' attribute bound to the same stableId property.
steps.hint: Use property binding syntax with square brackets: [for]="stableId" and [id]="stableId".
steps.expectedOutcome: The label and input will be programmatically linked using the stable ID, ensuring accessibility and proper form association.
successCriteria: Label element has [for]="stableId"
Input element has [id]="stableId"
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure both the label's 'for' attribute and input's 'id' attribute are bound to the stableId property using square bracket syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The label and input aren't properly connected. Remember to use property binding: [for]="stableId" on the label and [id]="stableId" on the input.

steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: adding a button with click handler
<button (click)="handleClick()">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button with the text 'Force Re-render' appears in the template, wired to a click handler method.
successCriteria: Button element is added to the template
Button has text 'Force Re-render'
Button has (click) event binding
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the button has the correct text and a click event binding.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't properly configured. Check that it has the right text and a click event binding.
